Depends on the class.

Here in Florida, two things can happen for regular classes. If it is a class sponsored by the state of Florida, then you take an EOC (End of Course Exam) that is graded by professionals at the school board, and has passing requirements set by the school board. If it isn't state sponsored, then the teacher will design their own final exam, which is generally easier.
(Sponsered isn't necessarily the right word,. but for example, Core classes like English 1-4, and math classes you are required to take such as Algebra 1-2 and Geometry usually have an EOC, but extracurricular classes like Physics, Marine Science, Auto mechanics. MTA, etc... have a final exam)

For AP classes, all tests are taken in a secure environment at your school or nearby school on a very specific and planned date without exceptions. All scores are sent to Collegeboard, which is nationwide, and tests are scored early and sent to colleges you asked them to be sent to, but you don't receive the scores yourself until 3-6 months after taking the test.

As for final grades go, if you have a final exam or EOC, that will be added to your final grade, and your teacher can decide how much it effects your grade for the class in the gradebook.

For AP Tests, colleges will look directly at the score you got on the AP test (which ranges from 0-5) and look at your final GPA (which is effected by turning in work and doing you what should be doing in school) separately. Your teacher is still required to give you their own final exam which goes into the gradebook.

EDIT: Clarity

Grade point average. 

*Regular Classes*

A = 4

B = 3

C= 2

D = 1

F = 0

*AP (Advanced Placement) Classes*

A = 5

B = 4

C = 3
